title: Can Elon Musk really put AI datacentres in space? - The Latest
summary: The Trump administration has approved Elon Musk’s plan to create datacentres in space. US federal regulators have authorised the launch of one million Starmind orbital satellites, which are built by Musk’s SpaceX, to process data in space. Supporters argue the project will be more energy-efficient and reduce the environmental impact of datacentres on Earth as the AI industry grows. But how realistic is the plan and what could the consequences be? Michael Safi speaks to Guardian global technology editor Dan Milmo Continue reading...

title: Young people are having less sex. What's going on? - video
summary: Sex among British adults has slumped in recent decades, with under-45s having half as many monthly encounters as in 1990 and one in three under-25s reporting that they have never had sexual intercourse. To unpick some of the possible reasons behind these declines, Madeleine Finlay hears from science editor and co-host Ian Sample. He tells her why young people might be having sex later, and what could account for the striking rise in women reporting that they don’t want children. Continue reading...
authors: Presented by Madeleine Finlay with Ian Sample , produced by Madeleine Finlay, Ellie Sans and Joshan Chana , the executive producer is Ellie Bury

title: Contraceptive pill usage in Great Britain fell drastically in last decade, research finds
summary: Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception.
